paragraphs: One-sentence judgment: this occupation is worth further verification only if you are willing to accept doctorate-level training, a regulated licensure path, ongoing work with uncertain clinical information, and the ability to hold the line between patient preferences and evidence safety.

Core output: turning history, symptoms, examination findings, and medication and supplement information into traceable assessment, patient education, monitoring plans, and necessary referrals, rather than selling the conclusion that natural means safe.

20 to 120 minute safe trial: using only a fully fictional case, organize the medication and supplement list and mark evidence gaps, interactions, red flags, and referral points; do not give diagnoses or treatment advice to real patients.

First threshold: first check whether the target region licenses this occupation, which examinations or prescriptions are permitted, who may sign, and when referral is required; a license in one United States state cannot be converted directly into a physician qualification in mainland China.

Naturopathic physicians (O*NET-SOC 29-1299.01) diagnose, treat, and help prevent disease using a practice system based on the individual's natural healing ability, possibly using physiological, psychological, or mechanical methods, and possibly using natural medicines, prescription drugs, foods, herbs, or other naturopathic methods.

This name describes a United States occupational classification, not a globally uniform license. The inputs are the patient's history, symptoms, examinations, medications, and goals, and the output should be a treatment record that has an evidence basis, stays within the authorized scope, is reviewable, and includes referral thresholds.

entries: History and medication verification: record symptoms, past history, family history, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, supplements, and allergy information.
Examination and evidence integration: complete physical or physiological function examinations within the license scope, and verify laboratory and imaging results and their limitations.
Shared decision making and education: explain the options, strength of evidence, possible benefits, risks, alternatives, and the changes that need to be observed.
Monitoring and referral: record responses and adverse events, and escalate promptly when red flags appear, problems fall outside scope, or another specialty is needed.

paragraphs: The work mostly takes place in outpatient clinics or independent practices, and may also involve remote follow-up. Common carriers include electronic health records, medical databases, laboratory results, medication lists, informed consent, and referral records.

Quality is not measured by using natural methods, but by a complete history, traceable evidence, identified risks, patients understanding the options, reviewable records, practice that does not exceed authority, and referrals that are not delayed.

The common key judgments are: whether symptoms involve an urgent red flag, whether an examination or treatment is within your own authorization, whether herbs and drugs interact, whether the evidence is sufficient to support a recommendation, and when consultation or referral is needed.

Responsibility boundary: before practicing, verify the license category, scope of practice, prescribing authority, and institutional authorization of the target jurisdiction; when red flags appear, scope is exceeded, or another specialty is needed, referral is required rather than handling it yourself.

The work loop in order is: collect history and medication information → examine and assess within the authorized scope → explain evidence and options → record the plan and monitor responses → refer promptly for red flags or out-of-scope problems. Occupational boundary: this occupation is not the same as family medicine physicians, chiropractors, or physician assistants, and similar patient contact does not mean the same training and authority.

Family medicine physicians: usually take on broader primary care diagnosis and treatment along the medical education, residency training, and physician licensure path; suited to people who want to enter the mainstream medical system and carry broader clinical responsibility.

Chiropractors: core training and authorization focus more on musculoskeletal and spinal assessment and manipulation; their license cannot be treated as authorization for naturopathic diagnosis and treatment.

Physician assistants: practice within physician teams or collaborative systems defined by law and institutions, with a different supervision and authorization structure; suited to people who prefer a team-based clinical path.

Selection signal: do not compare only that both help patients; compare the licenses available in the target region, daily outputs, evidence standards, prescribing or procedure authority, referral responsibility, and employment models.
Adjacent directions include: family-medicine-physicians, chiropractors

Break down the tasks first: generative AI exposure is not equal to actual adoption, automation probability, or job disappearance. The ILO task framework only supports item-by-item analysis and cannot invent a replacement rate for naturopathic physicians.

Editorial analysis (subject to data authorization and manual review conditions): better suited for assistance: organizing interview notes into a structured history, generating a visit summary to be verified, preparing draft follow-up questions, and comparing medication lists.

Editorial analysis (subject to data authorization and manual review conditions): retrieval assistance: can help form search strings and organize guideline or literature candidates, but citations, versions, study design, applicable populations, and strength of conclusions must be manually verified.

Editorial analysis (subject to data authorization and manual review conditions): risk screening assistance: can flag potential drug-supplement interactions or missing fields, but cannot replace drug databases, original records, clinical judgment, and authorized signature.

Editorial analysis (subject to data authorization and manual review conditions): must not be delegated to AI: independent diagnosis, issuing prescriptions, deciding supplement combinations, interpreting abnormal test results as no risk, handling emergencies, or deciding to delay referral.

Human control points: verify patient identity and source materials, confirm indications, contraindications, and interactions, check whether the action is within the license scope, have an authorized person sign, and carry out emergency escalation.

Data threshold (editorial suggestion): before use, verify the specific jurisdiction, patient information authorization, institutional systems, and tool terms; recording, transcription, and external model processing conditions cannot be evidenced by the O*NET software list.

Ability exercise (editorial suggestion): accumulate records around history structuring, evidence grading, interaction checks, scope judgments, and referral collaboration; no comparative study proves it outperforms text speed.

Insufficient evidence: no national occupational wage distribution for mainland China under the same scope as O*NET 29-1299.01 was obtained this round. The health and social work industry average is only a reference for lawfully established related medical care employer settings and does not prove that this United States occupation may practice in China.

In 2025, the average annual wage of employed persons in the health and social work industry in urban non-private units in mainland China was 146,266 yuan, and 75,631 yuan for private units. This is an industry category average wage, and the surveyed subjects exclude self-employed individuals and freelancers.

In the same year the average annual wage for this industry in urban private units was 75,631 yuan. Private and non-private statistics differ in coverage, unit attributes, and job composition, so the two figures cannot be treated as the low and high ends for the same person.

Insufficient evidence: no Chinese occupational wage distribution under the same scope was obtained this round; industry averages cannot be used to infer percentiles or individual income for this occupation. Verify the recruiter's lawful position, qualifications, city, contractual pay, hours, and benefits, and do not substitute a United States title for Chinese practice qualifications.

The O*NET wage table found this round uses the parent category 29-1299 scope, and no independent distribution for this occupation was obtained; the parent category combination is not treated as exact income for this occupation.

The O*NET 2025 parent category national wage quintile table: median annual wage 115,210 USD and median hourly wage 55.39 USD; both are centers of the employee wage distribution, not personal quotes or self-employment income.

The parent category 2025 annual wage percentiles shown by O*NET: 10th percentile 65,210 USD, 25th percentile 83,780 USD, 75th percentile 161,470 USD, and 90th percentile 195,190 USD; the range comes from a combination of various diagnosing or treating practitioners.

Coverage gap: OEWS is a survey of wage and salary employees of non-farm establishments and excludes self-employment; independent practice revenue, fees, and owner income cannot be directly compared with employee wages.

Region and license: state-level authorization scope, insurance payment, employment model, experience, and patient sources all change quotes, but the public parent category data cannot quantify each effect.

How to use it: treat the parent category statistics as a market anchor, then verify with the employer the base salary, productivity or revenue share, benefits, liability insurance, license fees, scheduling, and requirements to bring your own patients.

entries: Fit signal: you can patiently probe history and medication details and are willing to verify risks and evidence first, even when the patient expects a quick natural solution.
Compare the signals with specific work samples, supervisor feedback, and job requirements.
Fit signal: when facing incomplete or contradictory information, you flag uncertainty and ask about key missing variables rather than filling gaps with a confident tone.
Compare the signals with specific work samples, supervisor feedback, and job requirements.
Fit signal: you can explain the strength of evidence and alternatives while respecting patient choices, and do not turn consultation into product selling.
Compare the signals with specific work samples, supervisor feedback, and job requirements.
Fit signal: you are willing to maintain detailed records, follow-up results, and a closed referral loop, and can accept peer review and regulatory limits.
Compare the signals with specific work samples, supervisor feedback, and job requirements.
Caution signal: you treat natural as by default safe, or believe personal experience can replace checks of drug interactions, contraindications, and adverse events.
Compare the signals with specific work samples, supervisor feedback, and job requirements.

Caution signal: you are unwilling to refer when red flags appear, or you treat referral as professional failure. The safety competence of this occupation includes promptly acknowledging the boundaries of scope.
Compare the signals with specific work samples, supervisor feedback, and job requirements.

paragraphs: Caution signal: you are drawn mainly by the title or independent practice but are unwilling to invest in doctorate-level training, examinations, continuing education, liability insurance, and compliance records.
Verification method: personality labels cannot determine fit; use fictional cases, evidence retrieval, interaction checks, and referral explanations to have licensed clinical staff evaluate you.

Delayed referral: red flags, malignancy, or out-of-scope problems not escalated; the consequence may be delayed treatment; the controls are preset thresholds, same-day escalation, and closed-loop records. Interactions: herbs, supplements, and prescription drugs used together; the consequence may be reduced efficacy, bleeding, or other harm; the controls are a complete list, verification against authoritative databases, and follow-up. Practice beyond authority: cross-state remote services or performing unauthorized examinations or prescriptions; the consequence is patient safety and license risk; the controls are triple verification of the place of service, individual license, and institutional authority. Exaggerated evidence: treating a single study, patient experience, or the natural label as proof of effectiveness; the consequence is misleading shared decision making; the controls are evidence grading and explanation of alternatives.

Washington State example: RCW 18.36A.040 sets limits on treating malignancy for listed naturopathic modalities, while retaining provisions for consultation and treatment together with practitioners licensed under RCW18.57 or 18.71; the shared-care provisions cannot be omitted, nor can this be extrapolated to other jurisdictions.

Supplements are not a low-risk default: the FDA does not approve their safety and effectiveness before marketing, and there may be drug interactions, test interference, contamination, or adverse events.

Affected roles: practitioners and teams who identify red flags, arrange referrals, and track visit outcomes. Chinese diagnosis and treatment still requires lawfully obtaining physician qualifications and registration, and a United States title is not a substitute.

Possible consequences: delayed needed evaluation and treatment; emergencies are escalated immediately per procedure, and the time limit for ordinary referrals must be determined by need; record and track the closed loop.

Step 0: determine the jurisdiction of practice. First clarify the country, state, or province where you plan to practice, and find out the protected titles, approved education, examinations, registration, prescribing authority, and telemedicine rules; the path on this page is an editorial synthesis and does not represent uniform entry conditions.

Education judgment: the O*NET survey shows that 96% of respondents believe entry requires a doctorate-level degree, and this occupation belongs to Job Zone Five (SVP 8.0 and above), with another 4% mentioning postdoctoral training; actual requirements follow the target jurisdiction and employer.

Washington State example: submit transcripts from an approved institution, examination scores accepted by the board, and other required materials; the federal background check is submitted if required. WAC246-836-030 specifies the NPLEX biomedical, clinical, and minor surgery additional examinations; other jurisdictions must be checked separately.

Mainland China boundary: the Physicians Law of the People's Republic of China requires physicians to lawfully obtain licensed physician qualifications or licensed assistant physician qualifications, obtain a physician practice certificate through registration, and practice in medical and health institutions according to the registered practice location, category, and scope; United States naturopathic education or titles cannot replace that path.

Training evidence: practice history taking, medication verification, evidence retrieval, informed consent, records, follow-up, and referral in a compliant teaching or supervised environment, rather than conducting unsupervised trial consultations with real patients.

Work sample: use a fictional case to produce a one-page safety assessment: problem list, medication and supplement table, evidence level, risks, open questions, scope judgment, and referral thresholds.

Interview verification: ask about the position's credential requirements, clinical supervision, prescription formulary, referral network, liability insurance, electronic health records, privacy rules, performance metrics, and product sales conflicts.

Ability ladder: first achieve accurate records and no missed red flags, then evidence explanation and shared decision making, and only then independent judgment and cross-professional coordination within the authorized scope.

paragraphs: United States parent category 29-1299 background: BLS 2025—2035 employment 39,600 → 41,800 people, growth of 5.5%, and about 1,900 openings per year; this covers several kinds of diagnosing or treating practitioners and is not a standalone demand figure for naturopathic physicians or AI attribution.

Wage signal: the United States parent category and the Chinese industry proxy answer questions about different markets and different coverage, cannot be converted and then ranked, and cannot yield a globally uniform pay conclusion.

Regulatory driver: whether specific services can be provided is first constrained by local licensure, scope, institutional authorization, and referral networks, so there being demand does not mean a job seeker has a lawful practice path.

Safety driver: supplement use, interactions, and patient interest in integrative health increase the need for reliable information and risk communication, but therapy effectiveness or job growth rates cannot be inferred from this.

Technology signal: AI is more likely to change records, retrieval, and draft follow-ups first; employment effects also depend on system adoption, privacy, liability, clinical authorization, and manual review, and exposure itself is not a layoff forecast.

entries.answer: According to O*NET 29-1299.01, this occupation diagnoses, treats, and helps prevent disease using a practice system based on the individual's natural healing ability: collecting history and medication information, examining and assessing within the authorized scope, explaining evidence and options, recording plans and monitoring responses, and referring when red flags or out-of-scope problems appear.
entries.question: What do naturopathic physicians do every day?

entries.answer: Requirements vary by jurisdiction and cannot be presumed across states. Taking Washington State as an example, licensure and scope of practice are set by state law and administrative regulations: applications involve transcripts from approved institutions, NPLEX examinations, and background checks, and the scope of practice explicitly lists modalities that may not be used to treat malignancy. Other states must consult their current regulations and licensing board requirements.
entries.question: Is a license required? Are state requirements the same?

entries.answer: Cannot be equated with Chinese physician qualifications based on United States naturopathic education or titles. The Physicians Law of the People's Republic of China requires physicians to lawfully obtain licensed physician qualifications or licensed assistant physician qualifications, obtain a physician practice certificate through registration, and practice in medical and health institutions according to the registered practice location, category, and scope.
entries.question: Can I practice directly in mainland China?

entries.answer: No national occupational wage distribution precisely corresponding to this occupation exists. The National Bureau of Statistics of China publishes by industry category for 2025: the average annual wage in the health and social work industry was 146,266 yuan for urban non-private units and 75,631 yuan for urban private units; this is an industry average that excludes self-employed individuals and freelancers and cannot be interpreted as starting pay or percentiles for this position.

entries.answer: The main risks are delayed referral, drug and supplement interactions, acting beyond the scope of practice, treating a single study or patient experience as evidence of effectiveness, and misleading cross-border titles. Supplements are not reviewed by the FDA for safety and effectiveness before marketing as drugs are, and there are also interaction, test interference, and contamination risks; control depends on complete records, verification against authoritative databases, license scope judgments, and a clear escalation chain.

questions.answer: History and medication verification, evidence retrieval and grading, risk communication and shared decision making, records and follow-up, and scope judgment and timely referral.
questions.question: What capabilities are mainly needed to do this occupation?

questions.answer: No; the interest code only describes activity preferences, and fit should be judged from supervised clinical experience, preceptor feedback, and licensure requirements.
questions.question: Can the ISR interest code determine whether I am suited?

questions.answer: O*NET classifies this occupation as Job Zone 5 (SVP 8.0 and above); the survey shows that 96% of respondents believe a doctorate-level degree is needed, and another 4% mention postdoctoral training; actual requirements follow the jurisdiction and employer.
questions.question: What education is needed?

questions.answer: No, they are not the same. Washington State's license materials and scope of practice are set by state law and other states must be checked separately; a license or scope in one state cannot be treated as nationally valid.
questions.question: Are state license requirements the same?

questions.answer: It depends on state law and license category; some jurisdictions set a formulary or controlled substance limits, and cross-state remote services also require checking the rules of the place of service.
questions.question: How is prescribing authority obtained?

questions.answer: No; assessments are for self-exploration only and do not constitute evidence of licensure, practice, or hiring.
questions.question: Can assessment results serve as evidence for practice or hiring?

questions.answer: The current O*NET certification directory lists 2 associated certifications (oriental medicine Diplomate and classical homeopathy certification), which are not recognition of efficacy, uniform required credentials, or practice permits; licenses and examinations must be checked separately by jurisdiction.
questions.question: Which occupational certifications exist?

questions.answer: Red flag and referral pressure, the burden of interaction checks, scope of practice limits, and the difference between independent and employed practice.
questions.question: Which factors in the work strongly affect fit?

questions.answer: Keep supervised clinical records, case analyses, interaction check records, shared decision and referral closure records, and license and continuing education credentials.
questions.question: How do you accumulate reviewable professional evidence?

questions.answer: Use a fully fictional case to complete a one-page safety assessment (problems, medications and supplements, evidence levels, risks, and referral thresholds), and then ask licensed clinical staff for feedback.
questions.question: What kind of low-cost trial is best to start with?

signals.body: You are willing to patiently probe history and medication details, flag uncertainty with incomplete information and ask about key missing variables, can explain the strength of evidence and alternatives, are willing to maintain detailed records and a closed follow-up loop, and can accept peer review and regulatory limits.
signals.label: Fit signals

signals.body: If you treat natural as by default safe, believe personal experience can replace interaction and contraindication checks, are unwilling to refer when red flags appear, or are drawn mainly by independent practice titles but unwilling to invest in doctorate-level training and compliance records, this occupation brings substantial risk.
signals.label: Signals that call for caution

signals.body: Using only a fully fictional case, produce a one-page safety assessment: problem list, medication and supplement table, evidence levels, interactions and risks, open questions, scope judgment, and referral thresholds, and then ask licensed clinical staff to give feedback against real standards; do not give diagnoses or treatment advice to real patients.
signals.label: Low-cost trial

riasec_fit_block.fit_interest: Compare interest signals with real experience: whether you are willing to verify history and medications year after year, explain the strength of evidence, refer immediately when red flags appear, and accept regulation and peer review, rather than looking only at interest scores or self-labels.
riasec_fit_block.interest: O*NET marks this occupation's interest code as ISR: Investigative prefers analysis and inquiry into causes and evidence, Social prefers helping, teaching, and caring for others, and Realistic prefers hands-on work and concrete results. Interests only show which kinds of activities you are willing to keep doing and cannot predict clinical capability or practice qualifications.

components.work_context_block: Work context: mainly outpatient clinics or independent practices, and may also involve remote follow-up; common carriers include electronic health records, medical databases, laboratory results, medication lists, informed consent, and referral records. Quality is not measured by using natural methods, but by a complete history, traceable evidence, identified risks, patients understanding the options, reviewable records, practice that does not exceed authority, and referrals that are not delayed.

description.text: Naturopathic physicians (O*NET 29-1299.01) diagnose, treat, and help prevent disease using a practice system based on the individual's natural healing ability: collecting history and medication information, examining and assessing within the license and institutional authorization scope, explaining evidence and options, recording plans and monitoring responses, and referring when red flags or out-of-scope problems appear. This page uses only official sources to explain the occupation scope, tasks, preparation requirements, Chinese and United States statistical scopes, and authorization boundaries.
